newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cathay increases ex-France cargo rates.
newsitem.headline: Cathay increases ex-France cargo rates.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways said it had increased its ex-France rates by four to five percent to Hong Kong and onward destinations with immediate effect.
Cathay last adjusted its ex-France rates in December 1996, when increases of five percent were applied.
The Hong Kong airline was among several carriers operating from France which did not implement a fuel surcharge in autumn 1996.
The increases reflected the buoyant market at present on the Paris-Hong Kong route, a Cathay cargo official said.
The airline operates three Boeing 747-200 freighters each week from Paris-CDG airport to Hong Kong as well as a daily 747-400 passenger service.

Despite a strong level of demand, Cathay had no plans to increase cargo capacity on the route and this had been largely determined by the availability of aircraft and the priority given to other routes, the official added.
